title: When Protestants object, grave Romans excuse rather than openly damn—Bellarmino, Richelieu, Camus
source_text: LXXV. Praeterea hujus rei argumentum est, quod quum Protestantes ista objiciunt, viris in Ecclesia Romana gravibus, & magni nominis, ea nolunt aperte damnare; sed modis omnibus excusare conantur: ut videre est apud Cardinales, Bellarminum, atque Richelium. Et apud Petrum le Camus, Episcopum illum multitudine scriptorum, ante paucos annos, celebrem, in sua collatione cum Carolo Drelincourtio, circa honorem Beatae Virgini Mariae debitum.
pass_a_gloss: Moreover an argument of this matter is that when Protestants object those things, men grave and of great name in the Roman Church are unwilling openly to damn them; but strive by all means to excuse them: as may be seen in the Cardinals Bellarmine and Richelieu. And in Pierre de Camus, that Bishop famous a few years ago for multitude of writings, in his conference with Charles Drelincourt concerning the honor due to the Blessed Virgin Mary.
pass_b_english: Protestant objections meet excuse, not open damnation, from heavy Roman names.
Bellarmino, Richelieu, and Camus vs Drelincourt illustrate the pattern.

choices.english: strive by all means to excuse
choices.why: Shows institutional soft reception of extreme elogia.
